data.gender_notes: Maximilla is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Roman name 'Maximus', which means 'greatest'. In Christianity, Saint Maximilla is a third-century martyr who was a slave, and her name is a symbol of her great faith and dedication to God despite her difficult circumstances. The name Maximilla carries the meaning “Greatest” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Maximilla usually hope their child will grow to embody greatest and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes great faith and dedication to God.
data.etymology: Maximilla belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Greatest.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Maximilla total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

in_hebrew.name: מקסימילה
in_hebrew.meaning: השם מקסימילה נגזר מהמילה הלטינית שמשמעותה הגדולה ביותר
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם מקסימילה מקורו במילה הלטינית 'מקסימוס', שפירושה 'הגדולה ביותר' או 'העליונה'. זהו שם נשי שמשמש לעתים קרובות בקהילות נוצריות, ומיוחס לאישה שהייתה ידועה באדיקותה ובהתמסרותה לאל. השם משקף תכונות של גדלות, חשיבות והקדשה.

in_greek.name: Μαξιμίλλα
in_greek.meaning: Το όνομα Μαξιμίλλα σημαίνει τη μεγαλύτερη, την ανώτατη
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Μαξιμίλλα προέρχεται από τη Λατινική λέξη 'Maximilla', που σημαίνει 'η μεγαλύτερη' ή 'η ανώτατη'. Στην πρώιμη Εκκλησία Χριστού, ονόματα όπως το Μαξιμίλλα συχνά δίνονταν σε κορίτσια που γεννιούνταν σε οικογένειες ευσεβείς ή σε εκείνες που είχαν δείξει μεγάλο δέσιμο προς τον Θεό. Το όνομα αυτό αντανακλά την πνευματική σημασία της μεγίστης αγάπης και δέσιμου προς τον Θεό.

in_latin.name: Maximilla
in_latin.meaning: Maximilla, id est maxima, vel maximae magnitudinis
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Maximilla derivatur a Latina voce 'maximus', quod significat 'maximus' vel 'summus'. In primitiva Ecclesia Christiana, nomina huiusmodi crebro dabantur puellis quae in familiis devotis natae erant, aut quae magnam erga Deum devotionem demonstrabant. Hoc nomen reflectit spiritualem significationem maximae charitatis et devotionis erga Deum.

The name Maximilla encourages us to tap into our inner resourcefulness, courage, and determination, and to use these qualities in our service to God and others.

historical_references.reference: Maximilla of Trier (d. 451) was a Frankish queen and saint who is considered the first Christian queen of the Merovingian dynasty. She was the wife of Childeric I, the father of Clovis I, who is famous for converting to Christianity and becoming the first Christian king of the Franks. The early life of Maximilla is not well documented, but it is believed that she was born around 430 and was the daughter of Syagrius, a Roman nobleman in Gaul.
historical_references.context: Frankish kingdoms in Gaul, Roman influence

historical_references.reference: Maximilla of Thuringia, also known as Saint Magdalena, was a Christian saint who lived in the 6th century. She was the wife of Hermann, the duke of Thuringia, and is said to have converted her husband and their people to Christianity. After Hermann's death, Maximilla is believed to have ruled as regent for her sons, Gunther and Herman. She is venerated as a patron saint of Thuringia and is often depicted carrying a palm branch and a cross.
historical_references.context: Duches of Thuringia, Christianization of Germanic peoples
